label: Schlözer 1772 places colouring of Facta outside legitimate historical criticism and arrangement
subject: work.schlozer-vorstellung-universalhistorie.1772
object: Facta altered or rhetorically coloured by historian

sources.citation: August Ludwig von Schlözer, Vorstellung seiner Universal-Historie, part I (Göttingen/Gotha: Dieterich, 1772), pp. 44-45; ULB Sachsen-Anhalt Na 1135 d

observations.value: Zusammenstellung is assigned to the historian; its special manner constitutes Universalhistorie as method

claim_limit: Do not infer that Schlözer rejected pictorial, tabular or chromatic aids in general. The criticism targets intervention at the Facta layer.

label: Schlözer 1773 defends painted chronological display as a mnemonic for Synchronismus
subject: work.schlozer-vorstellung-universalhistorie.part2.1773

sources.citation: Herders Beurteilung ... mit August Ludwig Schlözers Anmerkungen über die Kunst, Universalhistorien zu beurteilen, Vorstellung seiner Universal-Historie, part II (Göttingen/Gotha: Dieterich, 1773), pp. [225]-416; locus p. 327
Modern study quotes p. 327 on gemahlte chronologische Tabellen, painted co-presence and Synchronismus through Association der Ideen

observations.value: Painted co-presence of already accepted historical objects can stabilize the relation of simultaneity without altering factual warrant.

claim_limit: Bibliographic location and pagination are secure; exact wording remains secondary-quotation control until institutional p. 327 is directly inspected. This is part of Schlözer's response to Herder, not the separate Species Facti quarrel with Gatterer.

label: Schlözer 1775 proposes table illumination to make world-historical duration visible
subject: work.schlozer-vorstellung-universalhistorie.1775
object: length and duration of principal world-historical periods

sources.citation: August Ludwig von Schlözer, Vorstellung der Universal-Historie, 2nd revised ed. (Göttingen: Dieterich, 1775), ULB Sachsen-Anhalt AB 22 A 9/k, 26 (1)
Modern study attributes to Schlözer 1775 the proposal that the length and duration of five main periods be made visible durch Illumination der Tabelle

claim_limit: The surfaced secondary quotation gives no precise primary page locator. Do not conflate this with the distinct 1773 p. 327 painted-synchronism passage or mark primary_direct before direct scan control.

label: Actor-level colour/pictorial jurisdiction in Schlözer: fact versus relation/display

observations.value: Schlözer rejects colouring Facta in 1772, defends painted chronological co-presence as a mnemonic for Synchronismus in 1773, and is secondarily reported in 1775 to propose table illumination for period duration. The legitimacy of visual/chromatic intervention is therefore layer-specific rather than governed by a general pro-/anti-colour stance.

Colour can be treated as an actor-grounded test of epistemic jurisdiction: what operation colour or pictorialization is allowed to perform, at which point in historical knowledge production, and under what warrant.

claim_limit: This does not establish that the Gatterer-Schlözer Species Facti polemic explicitly debated colour. The 1773 positive control belongs to the Herder controversy.

label: Directly close Schlözer's fact-versus-display colour/pictorial jurisdiction
notes: 1772 directly establishes the negative fact-layer boundary. The 1773 part-II work and p.327 locus are bibliographically fixed for the positive painted-synchronism passage, but exact wording still needs direct page inspection. A separate 1775 secondary quotation reports Illumination der Tabelle for period duration and still lacks a primary page locator.
reopen_rule: Inspect ULB Sachsen-Anhalt DOI 10.25673/95815 p.327; then search DOI 10.25673/95805 for Illumination der Tabelle. Keep the 1773 Herder controversy separate from the Gatterer Species Facti quarrel.

label: Gatterer human colour classification from Universalhistorie to Menschen- und Völkerkunde, 1771–1778
notes: A modern scholarly source cites Gatterer's 1771 Einleitung in die synchronistische Universalhistorie for bodily markers Statur, Gestalt and [Haut]Farbe used in human typification, indicating that the classifier regime begins before the 1775 Abriß der Geographie. The later Menschen- und Völkerkunde should be treated as a possible formalization rather than an assumed point of origin.
reopen_rule: Inspect Gatterer 1771 BSB/MDZ carrier bsb10716342 and the 1775/1778 geography editions. Record the exact headings and sentences for Statur/Gestalt/Farbe, what is being classified, and whether the operation is descriptive, comparative, geographic, causal or taxonomic. Do not project later racial categories backward.
